value.quote: Our main results are three polynomial-time approximation schemes
value.note: NP-hardness, inapproximability and approximation algorithms for computing the committee.

C1.reason: The results approximate the rule's own minimax objective, which the codebook assigns to AL (approximation algorithms for computing outcomes); they do not evaluate rules against a separate welfare objective, so WD does not apply.

value.quote: We say a voter v is satisfied with a subset T
value.note: Satisfaction is defined via Euclidean distances, and the same distances generate the rankings. The introduction's Remark also discusses how value relates to distance.

C4.1.reason: The paper applies 'satisfied', 'utilitarian' and 'value to a voter' to voters with ranking inputs, so C4.1 applies; the Euclidean model generates both the satisfaction notion and the rankings, which is a specified link.
